Welcome to Frappe CRM. If this is your first CRM, you're in good company. Most teams who start here were running sales from spreadsheets, inboxes, and memory, and that works fine until it doesn't.



In the next 15 minutes, you'll get your leads in, bring in your team, send your first email, and turn a lead into a deal.

## How it works, in one minute

A **lead** is anyone who might buy from you: someone who filled in a form, emailed you, or got introduced. You keep notes, emails, and follow-ups on the lead so nothing is lost.



When a lead gets serious about buying, you turn it into a **deal**. A deal moves through stages, from first conversation to proposal to **Won** or **Lost**.



That's the whole idea. Everyone on your team can see who's talking to whom, what was said, and what happens next.

## Finding your way around

Everything lives in the sidebar: **Leads**, **Deals**, **Contacts**, **Organizations**, **Notes**, **Tasks**, and your **Dashboard**. **Settings** are under your name at the top left.



![](/files/imagef535d7.webp)
*Sample leads in CRM*



Your CRM starts with some sample leads and deals, complete with notes, tasks, and calls. Click around and see how things fit together. When you're ready to start fresh, click **Clear Demo Data** in the sidebar.



There's also a **Getting Started** checklist in the sidebar. It follows the same steps as this guide and ticks them off as you go.

![](/files/udghamec6u-1.webp)
*Getting started checklist*

One quick thing before you begin: if you signed up with a login link, set a password in **Settings → Profile** so you can always get back in.

## 1. Get your leads in

Pick whichever way fits how you work today. You can use all of them.

1. **Add one by hand.** Go to **Leads** and click **Create**. Just a name and an email is enough to start.
2. **Bring in what you already have.** If your leads live in a spreadsheet, save it as a CSV. If you are coming from another CRM, then export from there the same way. Then go to **Leads**, open the **⋯** menu at the top right, and click **Import**. Upload your file, match the columns, and you're done. The same works for contacts, organizations, and deals.
![](/files/image2deeac.webp)
*Import leads via data import*
3. **Capture them from your website.** Go to **Settings → Forms** and click **New**. Pick the fields you want, publish it, and either share the link or embed it on your site. Every time someone fills it in, a new lead shows up in your CRM.

![](/files/imagee6c7ff.webp)
*Capture leads via webform*



Running Facebook or Instagram ads? You can [pull those leads](https://docs.frappe.io/crm/lead-syncing/meta) in automatically from **Settings → Lead Syncing**.

![](/files/imageb04f31.webp)
*Sync leads from Meta*

## 2. Bring in your team

A CRM works best when everyone who talks to customers uses it. Once your team is in, nobody has to ask "did anyone follow up with them?" again.



Go to **Settings → Invite User**, add their email, pick a role, and send. A **Sales User** works on leads and deals. A **Manager** can also change settings. An **Admin** can change everything.

![](/files/udghamec6u-2.webp)
*Invite your sales team*

If you have managers and reps, tell the CRM who reports to whom. Go to **Settings → [Sales Hierarchy](https://docs.frappe.io/crm/settings/sales-hierarchy)** and build your org chart — add each person and pick their manager, or drag them under one. This way, you'll be able to limit your users to specific data.





![](/files/imageb38e4f.webp)
*Reporting structure to limit visibility*



To share new leads out between your team automatically, set up a rule in **Settings → Assignment Rules**. Leads can take turns going to each person, or go to whoever has the fewest.



![](/files/imaged2b98b.webp)
*Assignment rule*

## 3. Connect your email

This is what makes your CRM feel like home. Once your email is connected, you can write to leads right from their page, and their replies land in the same place.



Go to **Settings → Email → Accounts**, click **New**, and pick your provider. For Gmail, Outlook, and most others, you'll need an **app password** instead of your regular one. The setup screen links to your provider's instructions.



Turn on **Enable Incoming** and **Enable Outgoing**, and mark it as default for both. If you'd like new emails from people you don't know yet to become leads automatically, turn on **Create Lead from Incoming Emails** too.



![](/files/imagee92192.webp)
*Setup your teams email account*



**Now send your first email.** Open any lead, click **Email**, write your message, and send. When they reply, it shows up right there on the lead, so you never have to dig through your inbox for context.



![](/files/image8ec818.webp)
*Lead with email communication*



Write the same emails often? Save them as templates in **Settings → Email → Templates**. And add your signature in **Settings → Profile**.

## 4. Stay on top of your follow-ups

Every lead has its own timeline, so the whole story is in one place. From a lead's page you can:

- **Add a note** to remember what you talked about
- **Create a task** so a follow-up never slips. All your tasks show up together under **Tasks**.
- **Leave a comment** and @mention a teammate to pull them in
- **Log a call**

As you work a lead, update its status: **New**, **Contacted**, **Nurture**, **Qualified**, **Unqualified**, or **Junk**. It keeps your list honest and makes it easy to see who needs attention.

## 5. Turn a lead into a deal

When a lead is ready to buy, click **Convert to Deal** at the top right of the lead's page. You can link it to an existing organization and contact, or let the CRM create new ones for you. All the notes, emails, and tasks come along with it.



![](/files/Screen Recording 2026-09-24 at 4.26.08 PM.mov)



Your deals move through stages that are ready to use: **Qualification**, **Demo/Making**, **Proposal/Quotation**, **Negotiation**, **Ready to Close**, and finally **Won** or **Lost**. Switch **Deals** to the Kanban view to see your whole pipeline and drag deals from one stage to the next.



![](/files/imagee7d341.webp)
*Kanban view: Deal pipeline*



**Set your currency first.** Before you add deal values, pick your currency in **Settings → Defaults**. You can only set it once, so it's worth getting right.



Once you've got a few deals going, the **Dashboard** shows you what's in your pipeline and what's likely to close.

![](/files/image299ac7.webp)
*Sales dashboard*



## 6. What next

When the basics feel comfortable, here's where to look next:

- [**WhatsApp**](https://docs.frappe.io/crm/whatsapp) and **Telephony** ([Twilio](https://docs.frappe.io/crm/twilio) or [Exotel](https://docs.frappe.io/crm/exotel)) to message and call leads from the CRM
- [**ERPNext**](https://docs.frappe.io/crm/erpnext) to create quotations and sales orders straight from a deal
- [**Custom views**](https://docs.frappe.io/crm/view) to save the filters and columns you use most
- [**Workflow automations**](https://docs.frappe.io/crm/automations/introduction): To automate your sales processes like lead scoring, reminders, follow-ups, etc.
- [**Mobile responsive:**](https://docs.frappe.io/crm/mobile-app-installation) Frappe CRM works in your phone's browser, and you can add it to your home screen like an app.
